extracted.intended_audience: NIH applicants, peer reviewers, Scientific Review Officers, and NIH staff involved in grant peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Authoritative NIH guidance describing the dual-level peer review process, review criteria, scoring, roles/responsibilities, and post-review procedures for research grant and cooperative agreement applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core values of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: The core values of peer review drive the NIH to seek the highest level of ethical standards and form the foundation for the laws, regulations, and policies that govern the NIH peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH policy is intended to promote a process whereby grant applications are evaluated on the basis of a process that strives to be fair, equitable, timely, and free of bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the five core review criteria and additional review criteria as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The overall impact score reflects the reviewer's judgment of the project's likely influence on the field and is derived from consideration of Significance, Investigator(s), Innovation, Approach, Environment, and any applicable additional criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance is one of the scored review criteria for research grants and cooperative agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers give a numerical score for this criterion (see Scoring). The criterion is considered when determining overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s) (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator(s) is one of the scored review criteria for research grants and cooperative agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess the investigators' qualifications and give a numerical score for this criterion as part of the overall impact assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation is one of the scored review criteria for research grants and cooperative agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate the novelty of concepts, approaches, or methods and assign a numerical score for this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach is one of the scored review criteria for research grants and cooperative agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate the rigor, feasibility, and appropriateness of the proposed methods and analyses and assign a numerical score for this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment is one of the scored review criteria for research grants and cooperative agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess institutional and resource support and assign a numerical score for this criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Protections for Human Subjects will be evaluated as applicable for the project proposed, but reviewers will not give a separate score for this item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered when determining scientific and technical merit and in providing overall impact, as applicable; reviewers also make recommendations concerning protections for human subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children will be evaluated as applicable but is not given a separate score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider inclusion plans when determining merit and may make recommendations regarding inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vertebrate Animals considerations will be evaluated as applicable but are not scored separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess welfare of vertebrate animals and may make recommendations; serious ethical problems here can lead to NRFC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Biohazards will be evaluated as applicable but are not given a separate score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider biosafety issues in assessing scientific and technical merit; serious problems may result in NRFC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resubmission will be evaluated as applicable but is not scored separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previous reviews and responses may be considered when evaluating resubmitted applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal will be evaluated as applicable but is not scored separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider progress and plans for continued support when evaluating renewal applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revision will be evaluated as applicable but is not scored separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes proposed in a revision are assessed as part of the overall determination of merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations (additional consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications from foreign organizations are an additional review consideration and are not given separate scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider any special issues associated with foreign organization applications but should not use these items in providing the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent (additional consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select agent issues are an additional review consideration and are not given separate scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety and compliance concerns related to select agents should be considered as applicable without separately scoring them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans (additional consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource Sharing Plans are considered as applicable but are not given separate scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans for sharing data, model organisms, and other resources are reviewed but not included in the numerical scoring of overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources (additional consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Authentication of key biological and/or chemical resources is an additional consideration and not separately scored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers consider whether authentication processes are adequate when assessing the application's merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period Support (additional consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget and period of support are additional considerations and are not given separate scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriateness of the budget and requested period of support should be considered but should not be factored into the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH scoring system (9-point scale and final score calculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses a 9-point rating scale (1 = exceptional; 9 = poor) for all applications; same scale used for overall impact and criterion scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each assigned reviewer gives separate scores for the five core criteria and a preliminary overall impact score. For discussed applications, eligible committee members provide final impact scores; the mean of final impact scores is multiplied by 10 to yield a final overall impact score ranging from 10 (high impact) through 90 (low impact). Not discussed applications are reported as ND (may appear as ++) and do not receive numerical impact scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not Recommended for Further Consideration (NRFC) designation
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be designated NRFC by the SRG if it lacks significant and substantial merit or presents serious ethical problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific NRFC reasons include lack of significant/substantial merit; serious ethical problems in protection of human subjects; or serious ethical problems in vertebrate animals, biohazards, and/or select agents. NRFC applications do not proceed to the second level of review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Officer (SRO) responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The SRO is the NIH extramural staff scientist and designated federal official responsible for ensuring objective and fair initial peer review and that laws, regulations, and policies are followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRO duties include analyzing application content, checking for completeness, documenting and managing conflicts of interest, recruiting qualified reviewers (authority in field, dedication to fair review, collegiality, experience, balanced representation), assigning applications to reviewers, overseeing administrative/regulatory aspects of meetings, and preparing summary statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer duties and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must declare conflicts of interest, maintain confidentiality, prepare written critiques using Review Critique Templates, assign numerical scores to each scored review criterion, and make recommendations on scientific/technical merit and other applicable areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers receive access to applications approximately six weeks prior to meetings; they evaluate protections for human subjects, inclusion, animal welfare, biohazards, and appropriateness of budget requests as applicable, and provide final written comments and numerical scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRG Chair role
rubrics_metrics.description: The SRG Chair serves as moderator of the discussion of scientific and technical merit and also serves as a peer reviewer for the meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair moderates discussion to ensure fair evaluation and may contribute as a reviewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and integrity obligations for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must maintain the integrity of the peer review process by not contacting reviewers, not sending information directly to a reviewer, and not accessing information related to the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are consequences for violation; see Integrity and Confidentiality in NIH Peer Review guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals grounds and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH established an appeal system to seek reconsideration of initial review results if the review process was flawed for reasons such as reviewer bias, conflict of interest, absence of appropriate expertise, or factual errors by one or more reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This appeal process does not apply to appeals of technical evaluation of R&D contract projects, NIH funding decisions, or decisions concerning MERIT award extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-level review factors (Advisory Council/Board considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Councils/Boards consider overall impact scores, percentile rankings (if applicable), summary statements, and the Institute/Center's priorities when advising on funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff provide a grant-funding plan to the council; council members may access applications and summary statements pending funding and conduct Special Council Reviews for investigators receiving $1M+ in direct costs to determine if additional funds should be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final funding decision authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Only applications recommended for approval by both the SRG and the Advisory Council may be recommended for funding; final funding decisions are made by the Institute/Center Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff and council advice inform the director's decision; IC funding strategies (e.g., paylines) and fiscal year considerations affect fundability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentile and ranking guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A percentile is the approximate percentage of applications that received a better overall impact score from the study section during the past year; percentiles are reported as whole numbers and only apply to a subset of applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary statements identify the base used to determine the percentile; ad hoc sections may use a different base. Percentiles and paylines are used by ICs to guide funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review applicant options
rubrics_metrics.description: If not funded, applicants may resubmit the application addressing reviewer concerns or submit a new application; applicants receive summary statements and are directed to Next Steps guidance and program officials for advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program officials listed on the summary statement can provide guidance; applicants whose applications result in awards work with program officials and grants management staff on scientific, programmatic, and budgetary matters.
